name: Atlanta & the Dirty South
blurb: The trap's home base — where 808s got darker, hi-hats got faster, and the tempo of Southern rap changed permanently.

artists.name: Gucci Mane
artists.note: Early trap-era Atlanta voice; helped define the genre's lyrical and sonic template alongside producers like Zaytoven.

artists.name: Future
artists.note: Popularized the melodic, Auto-Tuned delivery over dark 808 production that came to define a huge swath of mainstream trap.

artists.name: Migos
artists.note: Known for triplet flow (three syllables per beat) that became one of the most widely imitated rhythmic patterns in all of rap nationally.

artists.name: 2 Chainz
artists.note: Ad-lib-heavy, hook-driven Atlanta trap veteran whose delivery became one of the most imitated in the genre.

artists.name: 21 Savage
artists.note: Deadpan, menacing delivery that became a blueprint for modern Atlanta trap.

name: Memphis
blurb: Dark, horror-movie soul flipped into some of the eeriest, most influential low-end in rap — the direct ancestor of a lot of modern drill and trap.

artists.name: Three 6 Mafia
artists.note: The most influential group from the scene — DJ Paul and Juicy J's production defined the horrorcore-meets-rap aesthetic later cited by drill producers worldwide.

artists.name: Playa Fly
artists.note: Known for extremely fast chopped flows layered over the same dark, minimal Memphis instrumentals.

artists.name: 8Ball & MJG
artists.note: Foundational Memphis duo whose slow, bass-heavy style helped define Southern rap.

name: Bay Area (Oakland / Vallejo / SF)
blurb: Funk-bass-driven, uptempo, and unapologetically regional — hyphy and mob music built a scene almost entirely on its own terms.

artists.name: Mac Dre
artists.note: Considered the godfather of hyphy — his catalog basically defines the era's uptempo, bass-heavy party sound.

artists.name: E-40
artists.note: Longest-running architect of the Bay's slang-driven, bass-forward sound; also a key bridge between mob music and hyphy eras.

artists.name: 2Pac
artists.note: One of rap's most influential voices, came up in the Bay Area before becoming a defining West Coast figure.

tracks.title: 2 of Amerikaz Most Wanted (feat. Snoop Dogg & Snoop Doggy Dogg)

name: New York City
blurb: The birthplace — boom bap's sample-chopping, jazz/soul-sourced sound, and lyricism-first ethos still shapes what 'classic' hip-hop production means.

artists.name: Nas
artists.note: Illmatic is a foundational document of the sample-driven, jazz-inflected New York boom-bap sound of the early-to-mid 90s.

artists.name: Mobb Deep
artists.note: Defined a darker, grittier strain of the same boom-bap tradition — sparse piano/string loops over hard drums.

name: Detroit
blurb: Soul-sample chopping raised to an art form, plus its own rapid-fire, bounce-heavy street sound that's distinct from both coasts.

artists.name: J Dilla
artists.note: Producer whose sample-chopping and 'human' swung drum programming reshaped production far beyond Detroit — one of the most cited influences in hip-hop production generally.

artists.name: Danny Brown
artists.note: Blends Detroit's sample-based tradition with abrasive, genre-crossing modern production and a distinctly Detroit cadence.

artists.name: 42 Dugg
artists.note: Raspy, rapid-fire Detroit street rapper known for his distinctive slurred cadence.

name: Florida
blurb: From Miami bass's booming low end to modern Florida trap's especially chaotic, high-energy variant — a state with several distinct scenes.

artists.name: Uncle Luke / 2 Live Crew
artists.note: Foundational to Miami bass — booming 808s and electro-influenced uptempo production built specifically for sound systems and dancing.

artists.name: Kodak Black
artists.note: Pompano Beach — melodic but street-rooted delivery over that denser, harder South Florida trap production.

artists.name: Fie Scoobie
artists.note: Local Gainesville rapper, "Mr. Gainesville"

artists.name: 03 Greedo
artists.note: West Coast street rapper from Watts known for a melodic, gravel-toned delivery over dark synth-driven beats.

artists.name: Alemeda
artists.note: LA underground artist known for a raw, lo-fi rap-adjacent sound.

artists.name: 070 Shake
artists.note: Genre-blurring, half-sung delivery that helped define a moodier, more atmospheric strain of East Coast rap.

artists.name: 2 Pistols
artists.note: Mid-2000s Southern rap voice known for the strip-club anthem "She Got It."

tracks.title: She Got It (feat. T-Pain & Tay Dizm)

artists.name: 24kGoldn
artists.note: Genre-crossing Bay Area artist blending pop-rap hooks with rock and hip-hop production.

artists.name: 310babii
artists.note: Named for the LA area code, part of a new wave of melodic West Coast rap.

artists.name: 4batz
artists.note: Genre-bending Dallas artist blending R&B melody with rap cadence.

artists.name: 50 Cent
artists.note: South Jamaica, Queens street rapper turned era-defining mainstream hitmaker.

artists.name: A Tribe Called Quest
artists.note: Jazz-sampling pioneers whose Queens roots shaped the sound of golden-era New York hip-hop.

tracks.title: I Left My Wallet in El Segundo (Vampire Mix)
Bonita Applebum (Sir Piers and Si Ashton's Curious House Mix)

artists.name: Action Bronson
artists.note: Flushing-born rapper known for dense food/pop-culture wordplay over soulful, sample-heavy beats.

artists.name: 6 Dogs
artists.note: Part of Nashville's SoundCloud-era rap scene.

artists.name: 6ix9ine
artists.note: Bushwick rapper known for a chaotic, high-energy delivery and rainbow-haired persona.

artists.name: 71 NORTH
artists.note: Cleveland rap named for the interstate that runs through the city.

artists.name: 88-Keys
artists.note: Harlem producer-rapper closely tied to the 2000s New York backpack-rap and Kanye West circles.

artists.name: 99 Neighbors
artists.note: Unusual rap hub — a Vermont collective blending rap with indie and rock influences.

artists.name: 9lokknine
artists.note: Part of South Florida's aggressive, high-energy underground rap scene.

artists.name: A Boogie wit da Hoodie
artists.note: Melodic Bronx rapper who helped popularize a sung-rap hybrid style.

artists.name: A$AP ANT
artists.note: Member of the Harlem-born A$AP Mob collective.

artists.name: A$AP Ferg
artists.note: A$AP Mob member known for a chaotic, high-energy delivery and Harlem street style.

tracks.title: Beautiful People (feat. Chuck D & Mama Ferg)

artists.name: A$AP Mob
artists.note: Harlem collective that helped bring a fashion-forward, cloud-rap-adjacent sound to mainstream rap.

tracks.title: Put That on My Set (feat. A$AP Rocky & Skepta)

artists.name: A$AP Rocky
artists.note: Harlem's biggest 2010s rap export, blending Southern-influenced production with high fashion sensibility.

tracks.title: 1 Train (feat. Kendrick Lamar, Joey Bada$$, Yelawolf, Danny Brown, Action Bronson & Big K.R.I.T.)

artists.name: A$AP Twelvyy
artists.note: A$AP Mob affiliate from Harlem.

artists.name: Ab-Soul
artists.note: TDE member known for dense, wordplay-heavy lyricism.

artists.name: Abhi The Nomad
artists.note: Austin-based artist blending alt-rap with indie pop sensibilities.

artists.name: Abstract Mindstate
artists.note: Chicago duo known for soulful, boom-bap-rooted production.

artists.name: Add-2
artists.note: Chicago lyricist known for dense, socially conscious wordplay.

artists.name: Alex Wiley
artists.note: Chicago rapper affiliated with the Village collective (Vic Mensa, Chance the Rapper's orbit).

artists.name: Aesop Rock
artists.note: Dense, abstract wordplay pioneer of the underground/indie rap scene.

artists.name: Afroman
artists.note: Laid-back, comedic rap best known for the stoner anthem "Because I Got High."

artists.name: AG Club
artists.note: Bay Area collective blending punk energy with rap.

artists.name: Allan Kingdom
artists.note: Twin Cities rapper who gained wider attention via a Kanye West collaboration.
